metadata.boundaryMethod: Selected boundary is the mainland outline of hex-layouts/data.json (Census 2024 1:20m, dissolved districts), because the 1:10m county outline folds when the generator resamples it to 512 points; boundaryRings are the counties' own dissolved outline.
Arcs used by only one county of the group, chained into rings; largest ring selected for the single-boundary generator.

metadata.source: us-atlas 3.0.1 counties-albers-10m.json: Census Bureau 2017 cartographic county boundaries, 1:10m; 3,142 counties and county equivalents in the 50 states and DC (territories dropped).
metadata.projection: d3.geoAlbersUsa() with unchanged defaults, the same frame as the district file: the atlas's d3.geoAlbersUsa().scale(1300).translate([487.5, 305]) coordinates mapped exactly by (p - [487.5, 305]) * 1070/1300 + [480, 250].
metadata.coordinateSystem: Projected screen units; x right, y down.
metadata.representativePoint: Planar area-weighted centroid of all rings (the d3.geoPath centroid formula).
metadata.noAreaNote: These counties shrink to fewer than three points at the atlas's 1:10m precision, so they have no rings; their centre is d3's fallback (outline length-weighted centroid, else mean of points) and they keep their shared-border neighbours.
metadata.adjacency: Counties sharing a TopoJSON boundary arc: a stretch of border, not corner-only contact. No water connections.
